sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. The partner was invited to contribute by Towards Equality and Inclusion for their launch on 'A Review of Laws and Policies in Bangladesh for Empowering Left Behind Minority Communities'. This event was a step to effectively participate in the development process of Bangladesh Project at Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation. On the occasion of International White Cane Safety Day, ATN Bangla TV channel invited them to contribute towards a campaign on "Concept of International White Cane Day as Political Participation and Prevention of Violence against Women with Disabilities". Democracy International organized a Citizen Dialogue in Dhaka to gather citizens’ expectations including expectations of the youth people from diverse backgrounds. An initiative by Young Leaders from one partner organization was recognized by media during 2023. The published newspaper article brought attention to the SGBV issues faced by the gender diverse community in Bangladesh mentioning the work they are doing to support the community.

Capacity development programs

8 WRO and DRO organizations participated in a regional WGG learning circle on ‘Pleasure based Activism’ in 2023 under the counter-narrative strategy that enhanced their knowledge in understanding the importance of pleasure in feminist activism and its link with SGBV. Another partner organized a training on SGBV and Political participation to three DPO’s Representatives.
Original target was 8, which was revised to 5 for the year 2024. It is related to the capacity development programs.

In Bangladesh, several local organizations are working in grassroot level to empower women with disabilities and address the challenges they face. These organizations are part of the Women with Disabilities Development Foundation (WDDF) initiative through the WGG Activity, aiming to build capacity and create a more inclusive society.Five local DPOs are leading efforts in different regions:1. Uttoron Protibondhi Unnoyon Songstha in Dinajpur2. Joyeta Protibondhi Nari Unnion Sanstha in Shyamnagar, Satkhira3. Mohanagor Protibondhi Unnion Sanstha in Khulna4. Patnitala Disabled People’s Organization in Naogaon5. Nikunja Nari Unnayon Sangstha in Kushtia

Inception meeting with partners in Bangladesh with 25 attendees - providing a refresher on the ToC, project goals, M&E and WGG principles.

Two separate instances of two young women not being admitted into a technical vocational center and a school because of their disability occurred in 2022. They took the one of the strategic partners' assistance and using the guidelines stated in the National action plan on Personal with Disability Act they were able to secure admission.A college disagreed to admit a student despite high scores because the college did not have accessibility. With the partner org's support, the candidate was able to get admission in the college. On 18 Oct 2022, the Executive Director joined a National Media Workshop On Preventing Violence against women and girls with Disabilities and presented a key paper on how to prevent violence against women and girls with disabilities. Here Journalists made a commitment that they would raise awareness in society to prevent violence against women and girls with disabilities.

Cross movement meetings and dialogues

One of the strategic partners organized a roundtable on gender and climate justice to examine the intersection of gender and climate and how these contribute to SGBV and the resulting challenges in Bangladesh, on 6 September 2022 at a local hotel in Dhaka. 14 organizations representing UN, NGOs and INGOs, Women's Rights Organisations (WROs), and activist groups working on gender-centric climate change issues were present during this event. 2 Young Leaders organised a gender transformative workshop for the youth on 16 and 17 December 2022 with13 participants. The name of this event was ‘Gender Transformative Leadership in Action’. The training sessions at the workshop included discussion on topics such as Patriarchy, Sex-Gender-Sexuality, SGBV, Gender Discrimination in Daily Life, Allyship, Advocacy, and Activism followed by strategy, teamwork, motivation, advocacy, communication, and networking.2 Young Leaders started a programme called ‘Dignity In Diversity Program For Women’ with 15 participants. This is a 5 months programme that kicked off on 25 September 2022 aiming to empower marginalised youth from diverse gender, sexual and ethnic minority communitites in Chittagong through developing their capacities by enhancing knowledge on feminisms, leadership and movement to achieve sustainable goals.
Cross movement meetings and dialogues

Two partners jointly worked with Human Rights Commission on Anti-Discrimination Bill and submitted our policy paper to the Parliamentarian steering committees (committees on law, women and other) by post and email both by September. A media campaign (television Talk Show) was also conducted on “Leadership, political participation and barrier-free physical infrastructure of women with disabilities can help achieve sustainable development” . During July-December 2023, Young Leaders (YLs) from one WGG partner organization initiated two key alliances.
